qs.q: How many test runs and test configurations were recorded, and how many benchmark datasets does the suite have?
qs.a: 633 recorded test runs for 487 test configurations; 8 benchmark datasets plus 2 test datasets (three more in preparation)

qs.q: Under what licences are the tool and the datasets released?
qs.a: Benchmark tool GPL-3.0; benchmark datasets CC-BY-4.0 (the repository currently combines them; a planned reorganisation separates them)

qs.q: Can scores from different benchmark datasets in this suite be compared directly with each other?
qs.a: No. Scores are comparable across models within one dataset. Across datasets only after normalisation and with caution: the common 0-100% scale is for presentation and does not establish comparability between tasks or criteria

qs.q: What score does the presentation interface report for each dataset and model: an average, or something else?
qs.a: The best achieved score across all executed configurations (the maximum), not an average

qs.q: What does the framework explicitly NOT intend to produce?
qs.a: Generic leaderboard-style rankings or statistically representative performance estimates for the humanities as a whole

qs.q: Why are the datasets kept small?
qs.a: Expert annotation of complex humanities material is costly, and the aim is diagnostic realism and interpretability rather than scale or statistical representativeness; this also helps mitigate data contamination

qs.q: Do the authors treat the ground truth as absolute correctness?
qs.a: No. It is treated as operationalised scholarly interpretation, which makes evaluative choices explicit and contestable; domain experts produced or verified it

qs.q: Which single model performed best across all the datasets?
qs.a: NOT STATED. The paper gives no overall ranking (and says it does not aim at leaderboards); it reports best results per dataset

qs.q: What inter-annotator agreement was measured for the ground truths?
qs.a: NOT STATED. Ground truths were produced or verified by domain experts, but no agreement statistic is reported

qs.q: What was the average cost in dollars to run the whole benchmark for one model?
qs.a: NOT STATED. Cost is mentioned as something tracked over time but no figure is given
